column1: # boru Language Specification: Dispatch edge cases 3 — options maps,
# quoted-argument slots (QuoteArgs), arity forcing and 0-arg courtesy
# dispatch, guard-then-narrow on Any params, and undefined words.
# Four dispatch surfaces that sit OUTSIDE plain positional matching:
#   1. The Options pattern (EXPLANATION.md): a word's option form is a
#      separate signature with a trailing Map; longer arity sorts first
#      so the option-less call still lands on the shorter sig. Option
#      KEYS are not schema-checked at the plain-Map boundary today — a
#      typo'd key is silently ignored — but a Record-typed slot
#      (`refine Record […]`) checks keys, so schema'd options reject
#      typos at `make` and at fn params.
#   2. QuoteArgs slots: `def`'s name slot and `set`'s key slot take the
#      bare word AS DATA (even when the word is bound!), while `get`'s
#      key slot EVALUATES — an unbound bare key is an undefined word.
#      Dot access is a third rule again: the key is always literal.
#   3. The synthetic 0-arg fallback: a fn called with no collectable
#      args courtesy-dispatches its 0-arg overload when one exists and
#      raises a grouped-call hint otherwise. /N forces one arity.
#   4. An unregistered word raises [boru/undefined_word] — the /q, quote
#      and (quote …) escapes turn the SAME spelling into an Atom.
# §1  options maps — the optional trailing Map signature
